```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 6, fig.height = 3.5)
library(emaxProjection)
```

## Start with the scientific target

The target is the average **excess response over baseline** on a specified
linear dose axis. Its units are response units; it is the area divided by the
axis length. It is not the response at the maximum dose or the unrestricted
baseline. A valid inferential use requires fixed replicated doses, independent
Gaussian errors with a common positive variance, and the nonnegative closed
Emax model.

## Use observations or sufficient statistics

The following synthetic example is deterministic and uses no random draws.

```{r raw-example}
x <- rep(c(0, 0.5, 1), each = 4)
y <- rep(c(0.2, 0.6, 0.8), each = 4) + rep(c(-0.1, 0.1, -0.2, 0.2), 3)
region <- emax_region(x, y, D = 1, calibration = "contrast")
result <- emax_project(region)
result
```

No observations are excluded. Missing values and invalid designs cause an
error. A summary interface uses dose means, replication counts, and the pooled
within-dose variance. It cannot substitute a model residual variance or a
standard error for that variance.

```{r summary-example}
summary_region <- emax_region_from_summary(
  region$x, region$counts, region$means, region$pooled_variance,
  D = region$D, calibration = "contrast"
)
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(result$interval, emax_project(summary_region)$interval)))
```

## Read the diagnostics before using the interval

```{r diagnostics}
result[c("status", "converged", "termination", "endpoint_gaps", "width_bounds")]
plot(result)
```

Solid lines are outer bounds and dashed lines are feasible witness bounds.
The display shows numerical search progress, not a simultaneous confidence
band for the response curve. An empty intersection and unresolved feasibility
have distinct statuses. A budget-limited result must retain its diagnostics.

## Compare calibrations on the same data

```{r calibrations}
mean_region <- emax_region(x, y, D = 1, calibration = "mean")
mean_result <- emax_project(mean_region)
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  calibration = c("Contrast", "Full mean region"),
  lower = c(result$interval[1], mean_result$interval[1]),
  upper = c(result$interval[2], mean_result$interval[2])
), digits = 5)
```

The contrast region removes the intercept before calibration. Its ideal
projected hull is contained in the full mean-region hull. Independently
computed outer brackets can differ because of their finite endpoint gaps;
do not clip intervals to force a numerical containment result.

The [methods guide](methods.html) explains assumptions and boundaries. The
[reproduction guide](reproduction.html) distinguishes local package validation
from the completed manuscript study.
